newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai premier dismisses coup rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier dismisses coup rumours.

text.p: Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh reassured Thais on Wednesday that he was in control of the Thai armed forces and there would be no coup to overthrow his government.

Rumours of a military coup circulated late on Tuesday after Thailand announced tough economic reform measures on the advice of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The $12-15 billion package included three-month suspensions of 42 finance firms.
"I can reassure the public that the government has closely monitored the armed forces and there will be no coup d'etat as far as I am still in charge," said Chavalit who is also defence minister.

The powerful army, which has staged 17 coups or attempted coups since the country adopted a parliamentary system in 1932, also pledged that it would not use force to take over while Thailand struggled to overcome its worst economic turmoil in over a decade.
"A coup is an outdated action. The military will not do things not acceptable to the people and world community," army commander in chief General Chetta Thanajaro told reporters.
